# Code review: `ad6d5b9…f6cf22b` — ready to open the PR

This is a full review of the committed range you gave. The change is 1 file, +2 −1: `apps/mobile/src/features/Send/components/DialogModal.tsx`, base `ad6d5b9` → head `f6cf22b`. The worktree has two untracked folders (`.claude/skills/code-conventions/`, `docs/engineering/`), and they're outside this range.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Verdict** | Ready to open. Nothing blocks. |
| **Score** | **98 / 100** (1 finding, checked by the validator/refuter pair) |
| **What held it down** | No test would catch it if someone reverted the fix. Priority is low. |
| **Fix first** | Nothing required |

**What the change does:** it adds `accessible={false}` to the backdrop `Pressable` and to the dialog-card `Pressable`. Before this, VoiceOver and TalkBack treated the whole dialog as one element, so a screen-reader user couldn't reach the nonce or contact-name input or the Cancel/Save buttons. The fix is correct. It follows the pattern the repo already uses in 10+ places, including `SafeBottomSheet.tsx:144,163`, `InfoSheet.tsx:52`, `ConfirmationSheet.tsx:62` and `NonceBottomSheet.tsx:199`. Tapping outside the dialog still dismisses it, because touch handling doesn't depend on `accessible`. Screen-reader users can still dismiss it with Cancel, and Android users with the back button.

## Scores by area

| Area | Score | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Testing | 94 | 1 low-priority finding |
| Security | 100 | Checked: UI-only prop change, no data flow |
| Bugs | 100 | Checked: taps outside and `stopPropagation` behave as before; both consumers checked |
| Regression | 100 | Checked: `testID`s unchanged; no e2e flow reaches this modal |
| Conventions | 100 | Matches the existing `accessible={false}` pattern |
| Architecture, Performance, DRY, KISS | n/a | A 2-line prop change has nothing for these areas to check |

## Worth a ticket (not blocking)

**T1 · Testing · P3 · validator confirmed it, refuter weakened it (confidence 55)**
📍 `apps/mobile/src/features/Send/components/DialogModal.tsx:32,42`
- **What:** no test covers this change. If you revert both props, CI still passes. `DialogModal`, `CustomNonceModal` and `AddToAddressBookModal` have no tests at all.
- **Why it matters:** if someone later drops the prop, or wraps the dialog in another accessible parent, screen-reader users lose the nonce and contact-name inputs again, and nothing warns anyone. Root `AGENTS.md` says "Every code change must include tests."
- **Why it's weak:** Jest/RNTL (`jest-expo`) can't model how iOS/Android group elements for screen readers. A unit test could only check that the prop is `false`, which just repeats the source line. The earlier `accessible={false}` fixes shipped without tests too (for example commit `16a393ea4` in SafeBottomSheet).
- **Cheapest option:** a small render test for `DialogModal` that checks the children and both buttons render and respond to presses (`dialog-cancel`, `dialog-save`). The prop check itself could use `toHaveProp('accessible', false)`, as `SwapHeader.test.tsx:126-127` does for its accessibility label. Otherwise, add a Maestro step that opens the nonce dialog.

## Your call

| # | Item | Options |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | Add a `DialogModal` test | fix now · ticket · skip |

## Worth tidying while you're here

1 proposal, about 2 lines, and it doesn't affect the score.
- **C1** `DialogModal.tsx:57,65`: add `accessibilityRole="button"` to the Cancel and Save `Pressable`s. Screen readers can now reach them one by one, but they read them as plain text without "button". 40 other `Pressable`s in `apps/mobile/src` already set this role. Save's `disabled` state is already announced, because `Pressable` adds it itself.
- **Left alone:** wiring `onAccessibilityEscape={onCancel}` (the iOS "Z" escape gesture). No code in the repo uses it yet, so it wouldn't follow an existing pattern.

## Not covered
- I didn't check how VoiceOver or TalkBack actually behave on a device. No simulator was run, per your instructions (no tests, no installs).
- The two untracked worktree folders are outside the range.
- There's a `last-run.tsv` from an earlier review, but it covers a different range, so there's no "since your last run" comparison. I didn't overwrite it, since you asked for a review-only run.

## How this was produced
Scope was pinned to `git diff ad6d5b9…HEAD`. The repo profile was taken from the root and mobile `AGENTS.md` files. With a 3-line diff, I ran the nine area checks myself instead of spawning nine separate reviewer agents. One validator and one refuter agent then adjudicated the single finding. Nothing was edited, installed, run or posted.

| C1 | cleanup | Tidy | `apps/mobile/src/features/Send/components/DialogModal.tsx:57` (and `:65`) | Cancel and Save lack `accessibilityRole="button"` now that screen readers reach them |

For T1 and C1, reply with **fix**, **ticket** or **skip**. If you don't answer, I'll treat both as skipped.
